segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After they arrested Jesus, Peter followed at a distance and warmed himself by a fire in the courtyard, trying not to be noticed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A servant girl looked at him and said, this man was with him too. Peter said, woman, I don't know him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A little later, someone else. Then a third. Each time Peter denied it harder — I don't know what you're talking about.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And right then, while the words were still in his mouth, a rooster crowed.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Across the courtyard, Jesus turned and looked straight at Peter. Just looked at him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Peter remembered — Jesus had told him this would happen.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He went outside and wept bitterly.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the look wasn't scorn. It was the face of someone who already knew, and already loved him anyway.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He looked at Peter in his worst moment — and still chose him. He looks at you the same way.
